valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E per ADR (NYSE: BHP, USD), with FY2027 (year to 30 June 2027) EPS viewed at the 12-month target date (Nov 2027). Share basis: 1 ADR = 2 ordinary shares, per the cover footnote of BHP's FY2025 Form 20-F (SEC, 'Each American Depositary Receipt represents two ordinary shares of BHP Group Limited'); the ADR ratio is therefore applied as x2 to ordinary-share EPS. FX: none applied. BHP reports its results and EPS in US dollars, so ordinary-share EPS is already USD and the ADR values are USD without conversion. A dated AUD/USD rate for 13 Nov 2026 could not be sourced (RBA F11.1 CSV fetch was truncated and a second download was not permitted), and the ASX ordinary price is not used, so no AUD conversion enters the targets. Base year: FY2026 underlying EPS of 260.0 US cents per ordinary share (RTTNews, 18 Aug 2026, secondary coverage of the release), i.e. US$5.20 per ADR. FY2027 is set as an operating assumption, not a sourced consensus: copper guidance for FY27 of 1.65-1.8 Mt is below FY26 output and capex is about US$11bn. Base: FY27 EPS US$2.40 per ordinary share (US$4.80 per ADR) at 15x = US$72.00. Bear: US$1.90 per ordinary share (US$3.80 per ADR) at 11x = US$41.80. Bull: US$2.80 per ordinary share (US$5.60 per ADR) at 17x = US$95.20. Dividends are excluded from the targets (price-only basis). Ordinary-share and ADR prices are not otherwise mixed.

bear.driver: Copper volume step-down and weaker iron ore and copper prices cut FY27 earnings about 27% from FY26; the market refuses a premium multiple for a narrower copper growth path
bear.assumption: FY27 EPS US$1.90 per ordinary share (US$3.80 per ADR) at 11x

base.driver: FY27 copper guidance of 1.65-1.8 Mt sits below FY26 output, partly offset by record WAIO iron ore and the lower-cost structure; a multiple near the mid-teens for a diversified miner
base.assumption: FY27 EPS US$2.40 per ordinary share (US$4.80 per ADR) at 15x

bull.driver: Copper price strength and the Jansen potash start (mid-CY27) support earnings; the market rewards copper-led growth with a higher multiple
bull.assumption: FY27 EPS US$2.80 per ordinary share (US$5.60 per ADR) at 17x

valuation.implied_by_close: At base FY27 ADR EPS of US$4.80 the 79.49 close implies 16.6x (15.3x on FY26 ADR EPS of US$5.20). The MarketBeat consensus target of US$78.00 (10 analysts, as shown on 17 Nov 2026) implies 16.3x base EPS, about 8% above the base target; the gap is an EPS or multiple difference, and the analysts' assumptions are not sourced.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E on base ADR EPS moves the base target by US$4.80 (about 6.0 pp of the close). A US$0.10 change in FY27 ordinary-share EPS moves the base target by US$7.20 at 15x (about 9.1 pp of the close).
valuation.watch_metric: FY27 copper output and unit costs against the 1.65-1.8 Mt guide, and the realised copper and iron ore price. A copper run-rate below guidance or an iron ore price below the level implied by FY26 EBITDA of about US$33bn would weaken the base case; sustained copper output near FY26's ~2 Mt would support it.
valuation.next_disclosure: BHP Operational review for the quarter ending 30 September 2026 (already published) and the Q3 FY27 operational review (quarter to 31 March 2027, typically April 2027); the next full-year result is in August 2027.

analyst_notes: Only one named source with a verified date was found: Argus raised its ADR target to US$95 from US$90 on 28 Apr 2026 and kept a Buy, before the FY26 result, so it is pre-earnings. The MarketBeat consensus of US$78.00 (10 analysts, high US$95, low US$48, as of 17 Nov 2026) and the Yahoo aggregate mean of US$79.36 (7 analysts) are firm-level snapshots without dated named calls, and they disagree; both sit above the base case, implying a higher FY27 earnings or multiple view. Named ASX-listed targets from Motley Fool (Morgan Stanley A$67.50 Buy, Berenberg, UBS, JPMorgan, Morgans, Deutsche Bank) are denominated in AUD per ordinary share and were excluded because no dated AUD/USD rate was sourced, as were the undated Jefferies (Hold, A$68 from A$72) and Argus (A$60 from A$68) notes. The MarketBeat-cited BofA cut to US$91 from US$93 on 22 Jun 2026 was only seen in a search summary and is not entered.
